angles.drive: You see a chance long before anyone else wants it. Having somewhere next to go is your safety, so you watch where a thing is heading more than what it is. Keep looking that far, and accept seeing less of what is near.
angles.cost_self: Looking far comes naturally, and it pays. The next place is clearer to you than this one, so you see the far chance sooner than the near one. Check the opening at hand before looking past it, since that one closes on you most.
angles.cost_others: You look past the people closest to you toward the next place. Seeing far is how you keep them safe, and that gives the plan more of you than them. Let them share the view, since you see far enough for all of them.

angles.drive: A chance within reach is hard to leave on the table, because standing in place feels like losing. You take the one that is here rather than wait for a safer one. Keep taking them with your eyes open, since a few will cost you.
angles.cost_self: Taking the chance pays you more than waiting does. Moving makes you feel alive, so you put money into what moves rather than what is safe. Take the next one with money you can spare, since the wrong ones cost what the sure ones kept.
angles.cost_others: You take the chance for everyone whose money sits beside yours. Moving feels safer to you than staying, and you put their calm into the venture with your own. Let them size the next one, since the chance you take is theirs too.

angles.drive: A win only feels real to you once you have shared it. Providing is where you feel most yourself, and you share a good month out rather than put it away. Keep sharing, and know the price is a thinner cushion than you have earned.
angles.cost_self: Sharing the win is your natural generosity, and it leaves you short. What you give in a good year you lack in a lean one, because giving comes ahead of keeping. Keep some of each win back, since that is money you later go without.
angles.cost_others: You share each win rather than hold it until the next. Giving in bursts is how you love, and you give those you provide for plenty one year and nothing the next. Share in a shape that lasts, since they will come to you again.

angles.drive: The next chance always looks better to you than the one in your hands. Movement is how you feel alive, and you chase what is coming rather than work what is here. Keep in mind that you only keep what you stay to collect.
angles.cost_self: Chasing the next chance costs you the one you hold now. Each new start takes the strength the last one needs, and you would rather begin again than finish. Do not forget that the chance in your hands closes while you are off chasing.
angles.cost_others: You chase the next chance before anyone is out of the last one. You want starting more than staying, and you give the new venture what you owed the old one. You already know that you leave someone holding each chance you chase past.

angles.drive: You are spread across more things than any one of them can use. Saying no feels like losing, so you hold many small pieces rather than one whole thing. You give each one a part and none the whole, and that is worth remembering.
angles.cost_self: Spreading yourself thin keeps you from being caught out and keeps you tired. You give each venture enough to stay in rather than enough to win, since quitting feels like losing. Remember that you pay for all of them with the one body you have.
angles.cost_others: Wherever you can reach, you spread yourself across every person and plan. Keeping every option alive matters more to you than giving one your whole attention. Remember, you give each person in your plans the part of you the others left.

angles.drive: Starting a thing gives you more than finishing it ever does. The beginning is where the feeling lives, and you spend your strength there rather than on the last stretch. Remember that the half you did pays nothing until the rest is done.
angles.cost_self: Finishing is what you save for later. The last stretch asks more of you than the first, and you open a new thing sooner than you close an old one. Remember that the money and the credit sit at the end you walk away from.
angles.cost_others: You hand people a beginning and call it done. Starting is where you feel strongest, and you put everything into the first stretch instead of saving some for the last. Try to remember that you give the people waiting your start and somebody else's finish.

angles.drive: Reading the real value of things is your standing talent, and it works on houses, people, and offers alike. You see the water damage behind the fresh paint and the good bones behind the ugly listing. Bad deals rarely survive your first slow walk around them.
angles.cost_self: Everyone else toured the staged interior. You spent nine minutes in the basement with a flashlight and offered twelve percent under asking, with reasons attached. The sellers argued, then folded. Two years later the neighbors are still asking how you got that price.
angles.cost_others: Friends bring you their contracts the way people bring jewelry to an appraiser. You flip straight to the page where deals go wrong, and you are rarely wrong about which page that is. Your fee is a coffee, and the savings have bought several people cars.

angles.drive: Ground you have personally covered is your actual education. Markets, cities, kitchens, border towns: you learn places by standing in them, and every trip quietly becomes inventory. When a decision needs context, you usually have some, bought at the price of having been there.
angles.cost_self: The supplier problem stumped the office for a week, and you solved it with one call to a man you met at a trade fair in 2021, in a city nobody else could place. The office called it luck. Your contact list calls it coverage.
angles.cost_others: People assume your stories are exaggerated until they travel with you once and watch three strangers in two cities greet you by name. The network was not built at desks. It was built at long tables, and it keeps paying for itself in favors.

angles.drive: Plenty follows you around, and you spread it without doing the math. The garden overproduces, the table seats extras, the referral goes out before being asked for. Abundance is your operating assumption, and somehow the assumption keeps proving itself right.
angles.cost_self: You came back from the weekend market with too much of everything, again, and by Sunday night four households had bags on their porches. Nobody keeps score, least of all you. Somehow your own porch is never empty either, which you have stopped calling coincidence.
angles.cost_others: Around you, people relax about money in a way they cannot explain. There is always somehow enough, and some extra, and a plan for the extra. Scarcity thinking finds no soil at your table, and guests leave having borrowed a little of your assumption.

angles.drive: Wanting more ground is a hunger that eating does not fix. The bigger house asked for a better car, which asked for the second property, which asks nightly for a third. Each acquisition was supposed to be the last one. The hunger signs nothing and remembers nothing.
angles.cost_self: You opened the property app at eleven again, two years after buying the place that was supposed to end the searching. Saved listings: forty-one. The current house, by any honest measure, is enough. Enough has somehow never once felt like the finish line it promised to be.
angles.cost_others: Friends hear about each new purchase with congratulations that have grown slightly careful. They can see the pattern you narrate as progress: the goalposts move the week you reach them. Somebody once asked what amount would finally be enough. The pause afterward answered better than you did.

angles.drive: Staying put itches. Six months into any arrangement, your eyes drift to the exits: the next city, the next market, the next better setup. The moving was exciting the first several times. Somewhere along the way it stopped being motion toward anything and became the motion itself.
angles.cost_self: The boxes from the last move were still flat-packed in the closet when you started browsing rentals in a city you visited once. Your lease has eight months left. Your address book has three crossed-out entries per person, and your friends now write yours in pencil.
angles.cost_others: People love you from a slight distance, because the distance keeps changing. Invitations come with a built-in question mark, since nobody is sure which city you answer from this season. The freedom is real, and so is the pencil everyone writes your address in.

angles.drive: Your holdings outgrew your hands a while ago. The properties, the side hustles, the commitments across three time zones all technically function, and all of them get a thinner slice of you each season. Everything is covered. Nothing is tended. The difference is starting to show.
angles.cost_self: Sunday was for the rental’s leaky tap, the market stall’s inventory, the cousin’s business plan, and the neglected tax folder. Each got forty minutes and none got finished. You fell asleep mid-list. The tap is still dripping into a bucket that has its own schedule now.
angles.cost_others: From outside, your empire looks impressive, and up close it looks tired. Tenants wait longer, partners chase you for answers, and the best opportunity of last year slipped past while you were patching the worst one. Everyone can see the stretching except the person stretched.
